Here's what I have written up so far, other things might be floating in my head but this is what I got down to share first:
Countrya

States General custom government reform. Harpy Matriarchy is a monarchy reform that enables harem mechanics, and Countrya keeps this. However, the power struggle in Countrya society will be represented by a stripped-down States General where both sides still have a ruler for life and heirs and no elections, but the Federalists vs Monarchists influence bar is used. They will be renamed to Merchant-Matriarchs and Countryaese Matrons respectively, and will have different bonuses (and maluses?) for having them in power. Merchants might be economic plus corruption plus autonomy increases, Matrons might be religious power (more often using Hunt powers), autonomy reduction, and others. Repeatable events fire that detail the politics of Countrya, and just like with States General the player picks whose influence to increase and decrease. Staying too long at high influence for one side may increase the likelihood of negative events occuring. The conflict between the two sides is not resolved one way or another (such as into a true plutocracy) during a playthrough, but remains a constant struggle (or, "The Sway").

Why would Countrya adopt this kind of government? It retains their traditional matriarchy, but also includes concepts they pick up from their neighbors while demonsterizing. Verkal Gulan is a republic, but it was taken over by its ruling dictator by the start of the game in 1444. Countrya looks at this and says "We don't need to change much" when becoming a "civilized" government. The Raj is an old system where the Raja in theory has great power, but much authority is delegated out to the ministries, and the grand vizier. In addition, harimari ruling over humans is encouraging to see for the harpies, and they say they can do much the same thing (like Lax Rulers Harpylen idea) but mostly leave humans and others to their own devices in a demonsterized government. In all, Countrya looks outward for lessons on demonsterized government, and the somewhat humourous conclusion they reach is "You aren't that bad already all things considered." Therefore the rising Merchant-Matriarchs are added to their chamber of government, though the and the Matrons will continuously fight for influence over how best to apply Countrya Swift-Sparrow's philosophy.

Countrya.txt

Since the early days of Siadanlen, the followers and descendants of Mula Swift-Sparrow have been guided by her vision. Countrya, the nation that bears her very name, rose from the sands and soared aloft on her philosophy to outstretch its wings and now spans from West to East. Given the name "Talon-Queen" by her Ghankedeni family, Telarani did not wait for the ponderous advance of Countrya's diplomats and travelled far to make her own trade partners throughout Haless. She returned to the nation of her mother and claimed for herself the surname Golden-Peacock, for in all her spectacular adornments the most bedazzling were peacock feathers inlaid and expanded with gold leaf that were woven into her own plumage.\n\nOther harpies in Countrya had found themselves possessed of ever-increasing wealth and were beginning to form a cooperative power block. Telarani Golden-Peacock seized this nascent organization for herself, charming most, convincing many, and culling the rest. Many harpies of no standing flocked to them, seeking to emulate their success - Telarani's above all - and each of these "Peacocks" wore one feather themselves to express this aspiration.
